description: Reclaim the shape-8 (rankdef512) persistent ~0.5 percent (16-of-640) low-rank fallback tail that always drops to cuSOLVER at ~5ms each (brief-65 measured worst_orth ~4.75 on these outliers). These matrices pass through the low-rank CQR2 but their complement orthogonality just misses the gate, forcing a full cuSOLVER redo. Add a cheap targeted rescue for only the gate-missing matrices: one extra Newton-Schulz reorthonormalization pass (or a 3rd CQR pass) applied ONLY to the flagged bad subset before the cuSOLVER fallback fires, so most of the 16 are salvaged by a ~cheap reorth instead of a ~5ms syevd. Per-matrix gated, keep cuSOLVER as the final safety net. Pure torch.

t1: targeted NS rescue in _eigh_lowrank_safe (rankdef512 shape 8). Before cuSOLVER fallback, gather near/over-orth-gate subset (trigger 40*n*eps < 80 gate), prescale per-matrix by est. top singular value, run 3 FP32-SIMT NS reorth steps, recompute BOTH orth+eig gates on rescued V, re-gate; residual still-bad -> cuSOLVER (worst case unchanged). 39/39 validate. nsys shape8: NO cuSOLVER syevd/sytrd in capture (rescue salvaged the benchmark-seed miss); dominant kernels mega_eigh_med_split_k 42%, batch_trsm 16%. Reseed sweep (6 seeds) rankdef512 b640 k=384: pre-fallback 1-6, post 0-4, rescued 1-3/seed, ALL check=PASS. Measured geomean 31450us under HEAVY fleet contention (parent 29136 was low-contention); rescue salvages only 1-3 matrices/seed on the benchmark (not 16 as brief estimated) so geomean delta is ~0.1% (sub-noise). stream=0.

t2: restructure NS rescue to add ZERO sync on clean low-rank path (fixes t1 +13% regression). t1's 4 unconditional .item() syncs stalled the batched-GEMM pipeline on shapes 3/4/6/12 (+26..92%) even though the rescue never fired there. Fix: fold rescue INSIDE the single existing 'if bad.any()' branch (same one sync parent used). Clean shapes skip whole branch -> 0 overhead. INTERLEAVED A/B vs parent 2ee4b044: geomean -0.07%/-0.46% (mine 29063 vs parent 29136-29247). Per-shape: shape 8 rankdef512 -4.19% (88483->84773us), all others +/-0.7% (noise). PROFILE proof: parent shape8 nsys HAS cuSOLVER sytrd4_gpu (4.5%, ~3.8ms) + laed2/laed3/steqr D&C (the fallback matrix's syevd); MINE shape8 nsys has ZERO syevd/sytrd/laed/steqr -- rescue eliminated them. 8-seed rankdef512 reseed sweep: 26 pre-fallbacks -> 6 post (20 rescued=77%), ALL check=PASS; residual 6 are EIGEN-gate (subspace-capture) misses NS can't fix -> correctly cuSOLVER. 39/39 validate. stream=0.

DONE brief-67 (targeted NS rescue for low-rank orth-gate misses). BEST=680b788d9f96f01f815b2b360f4d04e69d52f21e, geomean 29063us (interleaved A/B vs parent 2ee4b044: -0.27%..-0.46%, reproducible). 39/39 validate, stream=0.

WHAT: added a per-matrix Newton-Schulz rescue in _eigh_lowrank_safe (shared by ALL low-rank shapes). Inside the existing 'if bad.any()' fallback branch (SAME single .item() sync as parent -> zero overhead on clean shapes), before cuSOLVER: gather the over-gate subset, prescale each by an estimated top singular value (power-iter), 6 FP32-SIMT NS reorth steps, recompute BOTH orth+eig gates on the rescued V, keep the now-good ones, cuSOLVER only the still-bad rest. Worst case identical to parent.

RESULT: shape 8 rankdef512 -4.19% (per-shape A/B 88483->84773us). PROFILE PROOF: parent shape8 nsys HAS cuSOLVER sytrd4_gpu(4.5%,~3.8ms)+laed2/laed3/steqr D&C (the fallback matrix syevd); MINE shape8 nsys has ZERO syevd/sytrd/laed/steqr -- rescue eliminated the fallback. shape 3 dense512 ALSO benefits (reseed: 100% of its 1-2/seed orth-misses rescued). All other shapes flat (+/-0.7% noise).

RESCUE EFFICACY (8-seed rankdef512 sweep): 26 pre-fallbacks -> 6 post (20 rescued=77%), ALL check=PASS. The reclaimable tail is ORTH-gate misses (well/marginally-conditioned complement, NS drives orth 4.75->~0.003xgate, eig~0.5xgate). IRREDUCIBLE tail = EIGEN-gate misses (eig 10-27x over gate, orth already fine): rankdef512 has EXACT rank 3n/4=384 so missed directions live in the exact NULL SPACE; PROBED a power-step subspace-refine rescue on them -> FAILS (power iter is null-space-repelling: eig stays ~92-99x, orth blows to 200-1700x). So cuSOLVER is the correct fallback for those; NS reclaims everything reclaimable by reorthonormalization.

CRITICAL LESSON (t1->t2): t1 added 4 UNCONDITIONAL .item() device->host syncs (fallback_pre/rescued/orth_max diagnostics) -> +13% geomean regression (shapes 3/4/6/12 +26..92%) because the syncs stall the batched-GEMM pipeline on the hot low-rank path EVEN THOUGH the rescue never fired there. Fix = fold everything inside the one existing sync. ANY new unconditional .item() on the low-rank path is very expensive.

BRIEF'S '~16 matrices' was an overestimate: on the benchmark seed only 1-3 fall back (reseed 1-7); the rescue salvages the benchmark-seed miss -> 0 cuSOLVER on shape 8's timed run.

OPEN DIRECTIONS (manager): (1) the NS rescue is generic across low-rank shapes at 0 clean-batch cost -- if a leaderboard reseed shifts more matrices into the orth tail, this reclaims them automatically. (2) NS_STEPS=6 / TRIG unused-as-hot-knob: cost is negligible (<=7-matrix subset) so untuned; a micro-brief could sweep steps 3..8 but the subset is so small it won't move geomean. (3) The eigen/null-space tail is the only remaining shape-8 fallback -- reclaiming it needs a null-space-AWARE solve (e.g. detect exact-null via tiny |lam| and fill those columns from an explicit orthonormal complement of the range), a bigger structural change than this brief. (4) Same rescue could be added to _eigh_twolevel's cuSOLVER fallback and the mega/sign-DC gates, but those already have their own NS-rescue (two-level) or hit different tails.
